newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says has complete faith in forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says has complete faith in forecasts.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard's office said he had complete faith in the August budget forecasts, despite his comment earlier on Wednesday that achievement of a fiscal balance depended on the economy.
"The prime minister has complete faith in the forecasts which underpin the budget," a spokesman for Howard said.
"He has no reason to believe they won't be realised."
Earlier on Wednesday Howard said on radio: "We do want to put the budget into underlying balance in year three if we can.
"I mean, these things inevitably get affected by economic activity and revenue flows and some of which are very hard to predict," he said.

"But whilst I can't bind the hands of the government in future budgets, I can say that we saw the target of those cuts in the first budget, brought down in August, we saw that as the kind of target we wanted to achieve."
He added that he was not contemplating another A$2 billion or A$3 billion in cuts on top of the announced A$7.2 billion.
The budget forecast a A$957 million underlying surplus in the fiscal year to June 1999, compared with a A$10.3 billion deficit in 1995/96.
The improvement depended on the economy growing as forecast and on a round of budget savings.
